source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of default parameters (PDF 47).

blocks.text: Function ke parameter ki default (pehle se tay) value ho sakti hai. Call mein argument na diya jaye to yahi value istemal hoti hai.

def greet(name = "Student") :
    return "As-Salaam-Alaikum,"+ name +"!"
print(greet( ))              # Output: As-Salaam-Alaikum,Student!
print(greet("Umer"))              # Output: As-Salaam-Alaikum,Umer!

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab return wali line baen margin par chhapti hai; yeh function ke andar indented honi chahiye, warna IndentationError aata hai. Doosri call mein "Umer " (aakhir mein space) chhapa hai, jis se output "As-Salaam-Alaikum,Umer !" aata hai; comment wala output pane ke liye "Umer" likhein.
Wazahat: greet ka parameter name default taur par "Student" hai. greet() bina argument ke bulane par "As-Salaam-Alaikum,Student!" aata hai; greet("Umer") par "As-Salaam-Alaikum,Umer!".

blocks.prompt: Default parameters kaise kaam karte hain, samjhaiye (short question 6).
blocks.explanation: Default definition mein likha jata hai (name="Student"). Agar call karne wala argument de to wahi value istemal hoti hai; na de to default, to function kam arguments ke saath bulaya ja sakta hai.

blocks.text: power function ka exponent parameter default (pehle se tay) taur par 2 hai. base badal kar Run karein: pehli call default 2 istemal karti hai, doosri call 3 deti hai.

base = 5
def power(number, exponent=2):
    return number ** exponent
print("power(base) =", power(base))         # exponent default 2
print("power(base, 3) =", power(base, 3))   # exponent 3 diya

items: Default parameter: argument na ho to default value (name = "Student").
